key_insight: PhysDial shows that learning from trajectories with changing physical conditions helps pretrained video models simulate how PDE systems respond to interventions.
engineering_relevance: More responsive learned simulators could support fluid-control and design studies that change forcing or parameters during a simulation.
method: Adapt a pretrained video diffusion transformer to eight two-dimensional PDE families.
Encode coefficients alongside noise level, condition fields as reference frames, and equations as text prompts.
Train on within-trajectory switches and evaluate predictions against changed solver branches from the same state.
evidence_signal: In Kolmogorov flow, within-trajectory switches comprised about 5% of training samples and halved post-change error at matched compute for forcing-wavenumber or amplitude changes.
watch_item: Results are limited to the tested two-dimensional systems, and reliable responses to new conditions may require targeted intervention trajectories.
paper_title: PhysDial: Adapting Pretrained Video Models for PDE Simulation under Changing Physical Conditions
